reason: A uses checked u128 digit accumulation so arbitrarily long numerator/denominator digit strings return OutOfRange instead of overflowing (B and D panic via unchecked fold), and otherwise implements the full R11-R16 check order correctly.

B completes patch parsing before source validation as R19 requires (A validates source first and can panic slicing a multibyte unprefixed body row) and correctly handles fuzz ranking, ambiguity and drift.

D computes effective priority by comparing age steps against the remaining headroom, avoiding the u64 overflow that A and C hit with priority + (now-ready_at)/aging_ms at extreme times, as R13 demands.

C validates snapshot names (NameInvalid) in restore/forget unlike B and rejects leading-zero negatives like "-01" in aggregate parsing unlike A, while otherwise matching the transaction/gc/snapshot semantics.
A validates host before port per R3 (B and C parse the port first) and rebases query escape offsets correctly (D reports query BadEscape/InvalidUtf8 one byte early at the '?').
C checks the creation parent via a full prefix walk so missing or file ancestors yield Missing/NotDir for the first offending canonical prefix, whereas A and B only inspect the immediate parent.
A rounds sqrt(d2*1e6) correctly with an adequate search bound, while B rounds up only when remainder >= 2k+1 (effectively floor) and caps its search below the maximum edge length.

A detects Missing for active packages absent from the catalog (B silently drops them) and validates lock names only after catalog duplicate checks (C validates lock names first), with correct exhaustive lock-cost optimization.
